question: The H.C.F. and the L.C.M. of two numbers are 25 and 250 respectively. If one of the numbers is 50, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of any two numbers is always equal to the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M.

Second Number = (H.C.F. × L.C.M.) ÷ First Number

⇒ Second Number = (25 × 250) ÷ 50

⇒ Second Number = 25 × 5 = 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

H.C.F. of the two numbers = 25

L.C.M. of the two numbers = 250

First number (N₁) = 50

**Formula Used:**

N₁ × N₂ = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

**Calculation:**

⇒ 50 × N₂ = 25 × 250

⇒ 50 × N₂ = 6250

⇒ N₂ = 6250 ÷ 50

⇒ N₂ = 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their H.C.F. is 1. For co-prime numbers, their L.C.M. is simply the product of the two numbers.

H.C.F. and L.C.M. of Fractions

H.C.F. = (H.C.F. of Numerators) ÷ (L.C.M. of Denominators) | L.C.M. = (L.C.M. of Numerators) ÷ (H.C.F. of Denominators).

Limitation of the Formula

The rule (N₁ × N₂ = H.C.F. × L.C.M.) is valid ONLY for two numbers. It cannot be applied to finding the product of three or more numbers.
